reason: The text explicitly depicts Moses and Aaron, the appointed leaders of the Hebrew people, actively taking accountability for the state of the Hebrew people. They are directly commanded by God to go to Pharaoh and secure the release of the enslaved Israelites (Exodus 6:13, 7:1-5). Moses and Aaron perform this mission: 'וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן אֶל־ פַּרְעֹה וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵן כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהוָה' (Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh and did as the Lord commanded). Rather than neglecting accountability, they directly intervene on behalf of the suffering people. While Moses initially expresses hesitation about his own qualifications, he proceeds with his assigned leadership responsibility.
